source_context: User requested a new v2 PM Bootstrap Planning Ledger for Feature: <provider updates> on 2026-06-24. Jared clarified that many provider specs are stale, with the first update focused on Gemini CLI being deprecated/replaced by Antigravity CLI (`agy`) and Antigravity CLI supporting multiple models beyond Gemini. Jared corrected the direction: kill Gemini CLI support, replace it with Antigravity, organize provider catalogs as Provider -> models like OpenCode, avoid stale Gemini CLI home override assumptions, and support thinking effort level selection for all providers/models. Jared later clarified Gemini Direct API is OK to keep, media support must be adjusted, and OpenAI(ChatGPT/codex) added ChatGPT Images 2.0 / GPT Image 2 / gpt-image-2. Broader media research covers image, video, TTS/audio, and music. Jared accepted provider-family grouping across vendors and answered `Both` for coding-plan and general media API route support. Jared then required no uncertainty: local testing must verify provider behavior, direct providers can use OpenCode repo/server evidence, and CLI providers must be tested. Codex and OpenCode are direct providers and do not need CLI bridging for core support. Current GitHub Copilot CLI hosted prompt execution is policy/subscription/license/admin enablement blocked. Cursor auth is route-specific. Direct Cursor Agent OAuth/session route is live-verified and freshly retested. Claude Code first-party session route is live-verified and freshly retested. Antigravity CLI `agy` 1.0.12 is now live-verified with model listing and exact prompt execution. OpenCode server 1.17.11 is live-verified as a direct provider for `opencode/big-pickle`; OpenCode-server-routed GitHub Copilot returns no text and server logs show `AI_APICallError: Forbidden`. Jared then clarified that `GitHub copilot likely isn’t working because I don’t have an active subscription.`, so GitHub Copilot failures are now classified as likely inactive-subscription/entitlement blockers unless future subscription-state verification or a successful prompt changes the evidence. Cursor route planning evolved: OAuth/session was temporarily primary, then Jared challenged whether that was only a CLI bridge and pointed to standardagents/composer-api as potentially more feature complete using a Cursor Dashboard API key tied to the Cursor subscription. Jared then provided a Cursor API key for live testing, explicitly said not to put it in the ledger, requested full Cursor capability testing, requested GUI helper text for obtaining the Cursor API key at `https://cursor.com/dashboard/` in the API keys section, and clarified that `opencode-cursor` is not needed because PM has native support. Native Cursor API-key / SDK / composer-api-style support is now live-verified for planning. Jared then asked whether Claude Code v2.1.80 status-line `rate_limits` is an issue PM needs to address and asked to update coding plans with full support including Qwen coding/Kimi. Claude Code `rate_limits` is accepted for usage/status planning. Coding-plan providers are now recorded as first-class Provider -> models routes, with OpenCode/Models.dev treated as source-lineage/catalog evidence rather than full support proof; live E2E support claims are blocked pending provider credentials/subscriptions. Jared then asked whether the newest OpenCode repo had been pulled for first-class provider implementation review. Current OpenCode `origin/dev` commit `b60c0a5e8ccc71ef7cce327602401418d419472e` was refreshed and inspected; OpenCode handles coding-plan providers mostly through Models.dev/generic AI SDK catalog ingestion plus transform rules, not bespoke adapter files. PM should use OpenCode as an architecture reference but own the provider/model transform mapping, especially Alibaba/Qwen `enable_thinking`.
